sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in Bridgewater, NJ?
sections.html:
A Bridgewater owner who needs speed can take a cash offer, list with an agent, or sell directly to a buyer they find themselves. In this township the listing route is strong, because prices are high and buyers are plentiful, so a cash sale is usually chosen for reasons other than price: a house that needs work, a relocation date, an estate, or a landlord leaving the business.

Bridgewater Township sits in the middle of Somerset County in the Raritan Valley, about 32 miles from Manhattan. The Census Bureau estimates 46,455 residents on July 1, 2025, up 1.0% from the 2020 base, which makes it the county's second-largest municipality after Franklin Township.

sections.h2: What does the Bridgewater housing market look like?
sections.html:
Bridgewater is among the pricier towns in central New Jersey. Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show a median owner-occupied value of $605,500, an owner-occupied rate of 84.9%, median household income of $172,851, and median gross rent of $2,176. About 16,505 households average 2.75 people, and 61.8% of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree. Median owner costs with a mortgage run $3,258 a month, so buyers are sensitive to taxes and condition.

The township covers 31.89 square miles of land and mixes older neighborhoods with large newer developments. It is split into recognized sections without formal borders:

  • Bradley Gardens, an older southwestern area with newer pockets and a commercial strip on Old York Road.
  • Green Knoll, the central area with Bridgewater Commons, the municipal building and the high school.
  • Finderne, in the southeast, with older streets, newer developments and TD Bank Ballpark, home to the Somerset Patriots.
  • Martinsville, the largest census-designated place at 12,147 residents in 2020, and Bridgewater Center in the west.

sections.h2: How do jobs, commuting and shopping affect Bridgewater buyers?
sections.html:
Bridgewater is the commercial hub of Somerset County. Pharmaceutical and life-science employers anchor the economy, with Sanofi's U.S. headquarters in the township, and Bridgewater Commons, a mall of roughly 994,000 square feet anchored by Bloomingdale's and Macy's, draws shoppers from several counties. The Census lists average travel time to work at 31.4 minutes, which fits a place where many residents commute out and many workers commute in.

Interstate 287 is the main limited-access road, Interstate 78 passes through the north without exits, and U.S. 22, Route 28 and Routes 202-206 cross the township. The Raritan Valley Line stops at Bridgewater station, and NJ Transit buses run to the Port Authority Bus Terminal (route 114) and Newark (route 65). Newark Liberty Airport is about 25 miles away. Buyers moving from New York or north Jersey often ask which streets are closest to the station and the highways, so put that in the listing.

Most of the township is in the Bridgewater-Raritan Regional School District, the largest in Somerset County, which also serves the borough of Raritan. It operated 11 schools and 8,254 students in 2020-21. The primary schools are Adamsville, Bradley Gardens, Crim, Hamilton, John F. Kennedy (in Raritan), Milltown and Van Holten; Eisenhower and Hillside are intermediate schools for grades 5 and 6; Bridgewater-Raritan Middle School covers grades 7 and 8; and Bridgewater-Raritan High School serves grades 9 through 12.

The township is also home to the Somerset County Vocational and Technical High School, a county magnet school, and the headquarters of the Somerset County Library System. Because buyers often shop by elementary zone, confirm the primary school for your street with the district before you advertise it.

sections.h2: What does Bridgewater require before you renovate or sell?
sections.html:
The township's Code Enforcement office administers construction permits and issues certificates of approval and occupancy after final inspection. A permit is generally needed for decks, pools, additions, garages, finishing a basement, new electrical outlets, and new or replacement furnaces, water heaters or air conditioning. A shed needs one if it is over 200 square feet or has utilities, a fence only if it is over 6 feet or serves as a pool barrier, and roofing only where sheathing is replaced. State law lets the construction official fine unpermitted work up to $2,000 per violation, which is why open or missing permits surface during a buyer's review. Plan review can take up to 20 working days.

Home fire safety requirements and applications are handled by the township's Fire Safety office. Call the main line at 908-725-6300, extension 5560 for construction questions and extension 5550 for fire safety, to confirm what a buyer's inspection will check. The municipal offices are at 100 Commons Way.

sections.h2: How are Bridgewater property taxes billed and appealed?
sections.html:
Bridgewater bills in four installments. The tax collector lists due dates of February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, with a ten-day grace period. If the lender escrows your taxes, the lender must supply the correct bank code to the tax office, and when a mortgage is paid off at closing the office should be told to remove it. The assessor runs an annual reassessment program, and each property must be inspected on a four-year cycle, so a visit from the township's appraisal contractor before a sale is not unusual.

ItemRule listed by the township
Tax installmentsFebruary 1, May 1, August 1, November 1
Grace period10 days, extended to the next business day if the tenth falls on a weekend or holiday
Assessment appealMay 1 of the tax year
Senior or veteran deduction claimWith the assessor October 1 to December 31 of the prior year, or with the collector during the tax year
Online payment fee$1.95 per e-check, 2.95% for cards

Source: Bridgewater Township Tax Assessor and Tax Collector pages.

sections.h2: What does the state charge on a higher-priced Bridgewater sale?
sections.html:
With a median value above $600,000, many Bridgewater sales exceed the thresholds in New Jersey's Realty Transfer Fee schedule. The seller pays the fee when the deed is recorded. For deals above $350,000 the rate per $500 of price runs $2.90 on the first $150,000, $4.25 up to $200,000, $4.80 up to $550,000 and $5.30 from $550,000 to $850,000.

When the price tops $1,000,000 for a residential property, a supplemental Graduated Percent Fee applies and the seller is responsible for it: 1% for sales up to $2,000,000, 2% up to $2,500,000, 2.5% up to $3,000,000, 3% up to $3,500,000 and 3.5% above that. The Division of Taxation posts the exemptions and forms, including RTF-1EE, on its realty transfer fee page. A cash buyer's lower price should be compared against these fees plus commission, not just the headline number.

sections.h2: What flood and site issues come up in Bridgewater?
sections.html: The Raritan River forms much of the southern edge, and the North Branch of the Raritan marks the western border. In August 2011, Hurricane Irene submerged the former American Cyanamid Superfund site, about 560 acres of which lie in the township, and chemicals leaked into the river. If your home is low-lying near the river, ask the township engineering office about flood information before you list, and keep any flood insurance and repair records for the buyer. The northeastern part, by contrast, is hilly because the First Watchung Mountain runs through it.

faqs.q: When are Bridgewater property taxes due?
faqs.a: February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1, each with a ten-day grace period. If the tenth day falls on a weekend or holiday, the next business day is the last day.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Bridgewater assessment?
faqs.a: The township's assessor page lists May 1 of the tax year as the appeal due date. Confirm the date against the notice you receive from the Tax Assessor at 908-725-6300, extension 5121.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a shed or fence in Bridgewater?
faqs.a: Only in some cases. A shed needs a permit if it is over 200 square feet or has electric or plumbing, and a fence needs one if it is over 6 feet tall or serves as a pool barrier.

The Bridgewater-Raritan Regional School District, which covers pre-kindergarten through grade 12 for Bridgewater and the borough of Raritan. The district reported 11 schools in the 2020-21 school year.

faqs.q: Does a sale above $1,000,000 cost more in New Jersey?
faqs.a: Yes. Residential sales above $1,000,000 carry a Graduated Percent Fee on top of the Realty Transfer Fee, starting at 1% of total consideration, and the seller is responsible for it.
